steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: You read or you are reading, one familiar listener.

action.note: For one familiar listener, use чита- plus -ешь: чита́ешь. Е follows a vowel here, with a short glide before its unstressed vowel. Final Ь is part of this verb ending; it does not soften the normally hard Ш.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: He reads or he is reading.

action.note: Use чита- plus -ет for he, she or a neuter it: чита́ет. The pronoun changes with the referent; this present-tense verb form stays the same.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: We read or we are reading.

action.note: For a group including the speaker, use чита- plus -ем: чита́ем. Compare the last part with the speaker form you heard earlier.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: You read or you are reading, plural or polite.

action.note: For several listeners or one polite addressee, use чита- plus -ете: чита́ете. This has one more vowel syllable at the end than the we form.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: They read or they are reading.

action.note: For they, use чита- plus -ют: чита́ют. Compare the end with the speaker form: чита́ю. The final Т belongs to the they form.

steps.instruction: Tell one familiar listener: you are reading.

feedback: Choose the matching familiar-listener verb ending.
action.success: Ты читаешь. — You read or you are reading, one familiar listener. Compare the parts, then try saying the complete word or message.

steps.instruction: Listen. Who is reading?

action.answer: They read or they are reading
accepted: they read or they are reading
action.reveal: Они читают. — They read or they are reading. Compare with your first answer. Replay or try again if useful.

steps.instruction: Write: we are reading.

action.reveal: Мы читаем. — We read or we are reading. Compare with your first answer. Replay or try again if useful.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: I think or I am thinking.

action.note: The thinking verb uses дума- in these forms, with the same endings as the reading verb. For I, add -ю: ду́маю. Its stress stays on у. You can keep the ending while changing the verb part.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: You think or you are thinking, one familiar listener.

action.note: For one familiar listener, use дума- plus -ешь: ду́маешь. Compare its ending with чита́ешь. Keep Ь in writing; Ш remains hard.

steps.instruction: Try a new combination: they are thinking. Keep дума- from the thinking examples and choose the ending used for they in the reading examples.

feedback: Keep дума- and use the same they ending as in the reading example.
action.success: Они думают. — They are thinking. You kept the thinking part and used the they ending. Listen to the complete model next.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: He thinks or he is thinking.

action.note: Use дума- plus -ет for he, she or a neuter it: ду́мает. The ending matches the corresponding reading form.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: We think or we are thinking.

action.note: For a group including the speaker, use дума- plus -ем: ду́маем. Compare the ending with чита́ем.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: You think or you are thinking, plural or polite.

action.note: For several listeners or one polite addressee, use дума- plus -ете: ду́маете. Compare the ending with чита́ете.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: They think or they are thinking.

action.note: For they, use дума- plus -ют: ду́мают. Compare with your earlier choice, then say the complete sentence.

steps.instruction: Address one familiar listener. Say: you are thinking.

action.reveal: Ты думаешь. — You think or you are thinking, one familiar listener. Compare with your first answer. Replay or try again if useful.

steps.instruction: Say about yourself: I am reading.

action.reveal: Я читаю. — I read or I am reading. Compare with your first answer. Replay or try again if useful.

steps.instruction: Write: she is reading. The he/she/it present verb form is the same in the taught pattern.

action.reveal: Она читает. — She is reading. Change the pronoun to она; keep the same verb ending as with он. Compare both words with your attempt.

steps.instruction: Say: she is thinking. Use the taught person and thinking pattern.

action.reveal: Она думает. — She is thinking. Change the pronoun to она; keep the same verb ending as with он. Compare both words with your attempt.

steps.instruction: Pause, repeat, or continue.

action.summary: You practiced reading and thinking with different people, changed verb endings, and built new messages. You can revisit one person at a time; there is no need to remember the whole set at once.

episodes.title: First windows into ideas
episodes.goal: Read four original micro-scenes with taught script; use short new meanings as supported bridges into mathematics, philosophy, fiction and science fiction.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: number.

action.note: This noun is grammatically neuter. It names a mathematical number. Stress the last vowel: число́; keep the two middle consonants together.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: one.

action.note: Stress the last vowel: оди́н. This is the masculine form of one. Here it names the number itself; its other counting and agreement uses can come later.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: One is a number.

action.note: This identifies one as a number. The dash links the named number to its description. Pause briefly there if useful; do not say a separate word for the dash.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: perhaps or maybe.

action.note: This whole expression means perhaps or maybe. Stress the first syllable of the first word. You can use it as a short answer when you are unsure.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: Is this a fact?

action.note: The naming frame becomes a question without adding an English-style helping verb. Listen to the whole question. To leave the answer open, you can use the earlier expression for maybe.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: This is a book. I am reading.

action.note: Imagine opening a book. Read the first sentence, pause, then read the second. You can keep the English meaning nearby.

steps.instruction: Listen, then connect this spelling with its meaning: This is a robot. It is thinking.

action.note: Imagine a robot in a story. The first sentence introduces it; the second says it is thinking. Он refers back to the masculine noun робот.

steps.instruction: Try reading the spelling aloud before revealing its model.

action.reveal_text: Один — это число. — One is a number
action.note: Try first, then listen. Compare one part at a time; you can replay and make another try.

steps.instruction: Listen to the short question. What is being asked?

action.reveal: Это факт? — Is this a fact? Compare with your first answer. Replay or try again if useful.

steps.instruction: Give the meaning of these two short sentences.

action.answer: This is a book. I am reading.
accepted: this is a book. i am reading.
this is a book; i am reading
this is a book. i read.
action.reveal: Это книга. Я читаю. — This is a book. I am reading. Compare with your first answer. Replay or try again if useful.

steps.instruction: Imagine a story scene. Identify a robot, then say it is thinking. Use two short sentences.

action.reveal: Это робот. Он думает. — This is a robot. It is thinking. Compare with your first answer. Replay or try again if useful.

steps.instruction: Imagine pointing to a sphere in a mathematical diagram. Identify it using the naming frame.

action.reveal: Это шар. — This is a sphere. Keep Это from the naming frame and add шар for the object in the diagram.

steps.instruction: Pause, repeat, or continue.

action.summary: You used the alphabet to read about a number, ask about a fact, open a book scene and imagine a thinking robot. Continue with short scenes that interest you, adding their new words and forms as you need them.
